name: moka (TinyLFU concurrent cache, with Mini Moka)
baseline: An LRU cache behind std::sync::Mutex (hashlink LruCache)
verdict_reason: Moka's TinyLFU policy does raise hit ratio, 4.5x over a mutex-wrapped LRU on the S3 trace. But a third-party mokabench run found its per-operation cost 7.3x higher single-threaded (Mini Moka 3.9x). It only comes out ahead when a miss costs far more than a cache operation.
tier_reason: Independent run (quick_cache's author) of moka's own public mokabench harness; CPU named, rustc not stated.
claimed_speedup: ARC S3 trace, 100000 entries: hit ratio 10.439% vs 2.327% for Mutex<LRU> (4.5x), but run time 17.728 s vs 2.422 s (7.3x slower); Mini Moka 9.399 s (3.9x slower). ARC DS1 trace, 1000000 entries: 14.907% vs 3.086% hit ratio, 74.586 s vs 8.901 s (ratios derived from page data).
workload: mokabench replaying ARC paper traces with 1, 3 and 6 client threads; a miss triggers an insert; no simulated miss penalty.
platforms: Any Rust target with std; sync and async (future) caches
one_liner: Caffeine-style cache with TTL and listeners; 4.5x the hit ratio of Mutex<LRU> on a search trace, but 7.3x the per-op cost.
how_it_is_fast: A count-min frequency sketch decides whether a new entry may displace the LRU victim (TinyLFU admission), which keeps one-off keys from flushing popular ones. Reads and writes are recorded in buffers and applied in batches to a lock-free hash table.
use_it_when: Misses are expensive (database, network) so hit ratio dominates total time
You need time-to-live, time-to-idle, per-entry expiry, eviction listeners or async get_with
skip_it_when: Cache operations themselves are the hot path and misses are cheap: a Mutex<LRU> or quick_cache was several times faster
caveats: Run in September 2024 with moka 0.12 by the author of a competing crate
Moka's own hit-ratio comparisons with LRU are published only as charts (moka v0.7.0)
No miss penalty in mokabench, which understates the value of a higher hit ratio
tradeoffs: Larger dependency tree than simpler caches
Eviction is approximate and asynchronous; size bounds are best-effort

evidence.quote: Benchmarks performed with [mokabench](https://github.com/moka-rs/mokabench) in a x64 Linux OS + Intel i9-12900H CPU.
